title: Shiksha Copilot: Teacher-AI Collaboration for Curating and Customizing Lesson Plans in Low-Resource Schools
extended_summary:
This paper examines how a generative AI-based lesson-planning system, Shiksha Copilot, was used by teachers in low-resource government schools. The paper is motivated by a practical problem common in under-resourced K–12 settings: teachers face heavy administrative demands, limited preparation time, multilingual classroom needs, and pressure to produce curriculum-aligned lesson plans for documentation and instruction. The authors ask how teachers collaborate with AI, what challenges arise when deploying LLM-generated lesson plans in non-English-medium classrooms, and how the tool affects teachers’ work practices.

Shiksha Copilot combined LLM generation, retrieval-augmented generation, human curation, and bilingual English-Kannada support. Lesson plans were first drafted by AI, then reviewed by expert curators, and finally customized by teachers for their own classrooms. The deployment involved 1,043 teachers across 757 government schools in Karnataka, India, plus 23 curators and 4 mentors. Teachers received training before deployment and then used the web-based system to access curated lesson plans, customize them, and optionally use chat and question-generation features. The study used a mixed-methods design with interviews, surveys, and platform log analysis.

The findings suggest that the system was useful for reducing lesson-planning time, easing bureaucratic documentation work, and lowering teacher stress. Teachers often used the plans as a starting point and adapted them using their own expertise and peer resources. The paper reports high reliability for English lesson plans, but substantial linguistic problems in Kannada translations, which required extensive human editing. More broadly, the authors conclude that AI can support teacher work in low-resource settings when paired with human oversight, but that multilingual quality, pedagogical alignment, and classroom context remain major challenges.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generative AI / LLM-based lesson-planning and teacher-support system used to draft, translate, curate, and customize curriculum-aligned lesson plans, plus related chat and question-generation features.
identified_tools.use_case: Shiksha Copilot was deployed in Karnataka government schools to support teacher lesson planning, bilingual English-Kannada content generation, curation, customization, and lesson-specific/general educational Q&A.

findings.finding_summary: In this mixed-methods deployment with 1,043 teachers and 23 curators, the system reduced lesson-planning time and eased bureaucratic workload. Teachers reported lower record-keeping burden and lower teaching-related stress; the paper also states that 85 of 5,542 teacher-created lesson plans (1.53%) and 19 of 1,480 Kannada-medium plans (1.28%) were modified on-platform, while most customization happened off-platform.
findings.measure: Lesson-planning time, administrative workload/record-keeping burden, and teacher stress (Teacher Stress Scale); platform log counts of edited lesson plans
findings.sample_size: n=1043 teachers; n=23 curators; survey analyses on n=406 matched responses

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods field deployment with surveys, interviews, and log analysis rather than an experimental impact study. It provides useful real-world evidence, but causal attribution is limited and key outcomes are reported without effect sizes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful practical benefits such as reduced lesson-planning time and stress, but no effect sizes are provided and the evidence is not from a controlled design. The low on-platform edit rates suggest adoption, but they do not quantify impact magnitude.
